letter.subject: Concern regarding continued tracking after rejection of non-essential cookies on reckitt.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://reckitt.com during an automated, passive audit carried out on 2026-11-08 04:07 UTC. Using a fresh browser session, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked the option “Reject Non-Essential Cookies”, then browsed the site and recorded what was still sent afterwards.

The pages browsed after rejection were:
1. https://www.reckitt.com/our-company/
2. https://www.reckitt.com/news/from-a-simple-scientific-question-to-the-worlds-go-to-heartburn-indigestion-brand/
3. https://www.reckitt.com/brands/

Your privacy policy reviewed during this process was: https://www.reckitt.com/privacy-policy/

The issues identified were:
1. Our review suggests that advertising trackers continued after cookies were rejected. After the reject option was successfully clicked, requests to Google Tag Manager and Microsoft Clarity still continued while further pages were browsed. This appears to conflict with the site’s stated approach that cookies are placed only after consent, particularly for advertising purposes.
2. Microsoft still received data after cookies were rejected. We observed 15 requests to clarity.ms after the reject choice was clicked.
3. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. We observed 5 requests to googletagmanager.com after the reject choice was clicked.

In light of the above, please:
1. Explain each of the points above, including the purpose of the relevant requests and why they continued after rejection.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers or related technologies you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and the basis on which you consider them to be so.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit found a cookie banner with a successfully used rejection option, but advertising-related requests to Google Tag Manager and Microsoft Clarity continued afterwards. This appears to conflict directly with the cookie policy's statement that cookies are placed after consent. The privacy and cookie policies cover the main UK GDPR information categories, although the observed behaviour raises a serious transparency and consent concern.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: True. Method: selector. Buttons clicked: Reject Non-Essential​ Cookies.

E2: Tracker Google (Advertising): 1 requests before consent, 5 after reject, to googletagmanager.com. Example after-reject requests: https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-NQ4QD9 | https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-NQ4QD9

E3: Tracker Microsoft (Advertising): 3 requests before consent, 15 after reject, to clarity.ms. Example after-reject requests: https://www.clarity.ms/tag/hz22vplcuh | https://scripts.clarity.ms/0.8.77-beta/clarity.js

E4: Pages browsed and scrolled after reject: https://www.reckitt.com/our-company/, https://www.reckitt.com/news/from-a-simple-scientific-question-to-the-worlds-go-to-heartburn-indigestion-brand/, https://www.reckitt.com/brands/.
E5: Privacy policy: https://www.reckitt.com/privacy-policy/. Companies it names: Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok. Contact email found: PrivacyOffice@reckitt.com.
E7: Automated check (high): Microsoft still received data after you rejected cookies. 15 requests to clarity.ms after you clicked reject (Advertising).
E8: Automated check (high): Google still received data after you rejected cookies. 5 requests to googletagmanager.com after you clicked reject (Advertising).
